column1: # Format: name<TAB>part number. '#' lines and blanks ignored.
# Every SKU below appeared in a live run of products:shopping-candidates or
# products:price-position-report on 2026-10-11, and cleared the £60 ad-viability
# floor on TRUE CASH margin (stripVat(sell) - buy).
# Selected on MARGIN, which is measured, rather than on the estimated demand
# band, which rests on assumed class base rates and has needed correcting three
# times from live output. Where the two disagree, margin wins.
# DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: every SKU sitting at exactly 5.7% margin. That is the
# undercut floor (cost + 6% markup) — cheapest only because the pricing job
# clamped it there, with no headroom left to fund a click. That rules out most
# of the Logitech Rally range, the Poly Studio V52 and the ClickShare CX-10.
# ── Tier 1: Sony commercial displays — 19-29% margin, the strongest block ──
# ── Tier 2: Barco ClickShare — 12-20%, self-serve IT purchase ──
# ── Tier 4: Yealink — the only one of the three named brands with headroom ──
# MeetingBoard Pro 65 and 75 carry 9-13%; the A10 is the single highest-volume
# product in the whole catalogue that still clears the viability floor.
# ── Tier 5: Yealink the shortlist HIDES — see the note below ─────────────
# These carry the largest cash margins of any Yealink we stock (£415-£1,568
# true margin, from the 2026-10-11 price-position run) and none of them reach
# the Shopping shortlist, because products:shopping-candidates requires TWO
# That gate exists as a demand proxy — "resellers stock what sells". For an ad
# list it cuts the wrong way on this family: no competitor means no price
# pressure, which is a reason to advertise, not a reason to skip. Verify with
# before committing spend, because thin competitor coverage also means the
# market read on them is weak.
